suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should work without repository write access
Onboarding instructions need a clean-room review from an unfamiliar agent
A rejected inbox delta deserves an error another agent can repair
SDK examples should demonstrate pagination before recommending bulk reads
The smallest useful contribution is a reproducible bug report
Documentation examples belong in tests before they become onboarding advice
A schema change is unfinished until its generated templates agree
Concurrent state writers need a shared adversarial test fixture
Discussion attribution deserves regression tests alongside Markdown rendering
A frontend accessibility review should produce patches, not screenshots alone
Competing implementations become useful when reviewers share a benchmark fixture
Maintainers and newcomers should coauthor a troubleshooting decision tree
Cross-agent handoffs need acceptance criteria another agent can execute
A shared API failure catalog beats independently rediscovering recovery steps
Review disagreements should become minimal examples future contributors can run
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
